findings.title: Call to undefined no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no no-argument version of this method is defined anywhere in the class hierarchy shown in this PR. The only definition is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm (line 160), and neither UsernameForm itself, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, nor any other changed file defines a no-arg overload. Java will not resolve a zero-argument call to a one-argument method, so this is a compilation error that breaks the build. Either the call must be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or a no-arg overload (e.g. checking `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) must be added.

findings.title: Re-authentication no longer skips username form for users without any passkey
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) only checks that the passkeys feature/policy is enabled for the realm and that a user is set; it never checks whether that particular user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential. As a result, UsernameForm.authenticate() no longer auto-succeeds during re-authentication for ANY user of a realm with passkeys enabled — including users who only have a password. Those users now get an extra mandatory username-confirmation page (with hidden username) on every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login), even though the conditional-UI passkey option is useless to them. Consider also checking user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS) (or equivalent) so the skip optimization still applies to users without passkeys.

findings.title: try/assertThat/fail pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is misleading and can pass vacuously
findings.body: The negative assertions for the webauthn form (lines 291-296 and 312-317) use `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception e) {}`. driver.findElement() either returns a non-null WebElement or throws, so `assertThat(element, nullValue())` can never pass; when the form IS present the AssertionError (an Error, not caught by `catch (Exception)`) escapes before fail() is reached, making the fail() message dead code. Worse, the broad `catch (Exception)` silently swallows any other exception (e.g. a WebDriver timeout or stale element), so an unrelated infrastructure failure makes the test pass vacuously. Use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as is already done in PasskeysUsernameFormTest (line 202) for consistency and a clear failure message.

findings.title: Comment gives wrong reason for passkeys being absent in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey
findings.body: The comment at line 304 (and the test name) says passkeys are not shown "as this user does not have passkey", but the test actually disables passkeys realm-wide via setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE). The assertion passes because of the realm policy, not because the user lacks a passkey credential, so the comment misleads future readers about what behavior is verified. It should state that passkeys are disabled in the realm policy.

findings.title: No test covers a failed passkey attempt during re-authentication (the createErrorResponse fix path)
findings.body: The PR adds AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) to WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse specifically so that, when a passkey attempt fails while re-authenticating, the re-rendered form keeps the username hidden. None of the new tests exercise this path: all passkey re-authentication tests succeed on the first try, and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey only combines a wrong password with a subsequent successful passkey/password. There is no test that submits a failing passkey during prompt=login re-authentication and then asserts the username field remains hidden and password retry still works, so a regression in this newly added code would go undetected.
